critique_of_gto_peer: GTO Theoretician runs the equity-realization math cleanly: raw ~22-25%, realization 0.85 in 3-way going pot, reverse-implied collapse to ~17-19% vs ~22% required. Their 90/10 FOLD mix is slightly too pure; they under-weight the small-sizing (~22% pot) defending grid which mathematically pulls AJo back toward the bottom of BB's continue at this price. Their per-villain range chain (UTG narrowed to overpairs+Tx, HJ/CO capped to Tx/mid-PP/SD) matches my construction and confirms AJo unblocks little of value and blocks little of villain bluff.
critique_of_multiway_peer: Multiway Specialist correctly identifies the dominant structural factor: OOP-3-deep negative realization plus 0.75 4-way realization factor. Their point that closing-action benefit is single-street only is a key correction to the naive 'closing action saves it' temptation that Sonnet labellers 1/3 leaned on. Their reverse-implied analysis (J-turn into QJ/KJ/JT 2-pair, A-turn into AT/AK) crystallises why the 6 'clean' outs are actually dirty. Pure-FOLD with <10% CALL is defensible but slightly tighter than the small-sizing defending grid warrants.
critique_of_sonnet_majority: Three CALL labels (1, 2, 3) all anchor on pot odds (~18% required), 6 overcard outs, A-blocker, and BDFD/BDSD. Labellers 1 and 2 explicitly invoke backdoor-flush equity, but BDFD on a true rainbow with only the Ad is essentially zero (only one suit has any backdoor leg) — this is a real range-construction miscount. Labeller 3 invents a 'gutshot to nut straight' that doesn't exist on T64 with AJ (no straight draw at all) and conflates A-blocker EV with realised EV. The CALL argument quality is mediocre: pot-odds plus blocker arithmetic without honest reverse-implied or realization haircut. All three under-weight the OOP-3-deep cost.
critique_of_opus_tierup: Opus FOLD MEDIUM correctly identifies structural OOP-early squeeze-pressure-asymmetry (HJ/CO can raise behind), recognises realization deficit pushes required equity from 18% face-value to ~28-30%, and notes turn-cards make overcards dirty rather than clean. Opus keeps MEDIUM (not HIGH) confidence because the 22% sizing genuinely defendability-floors AJ on the BB defending grid — this is the honest calibration and matches my view better than either peer's HIGH. Opus's verdict is the strongest single-label anchor in this debate.
revised_reasoning: Round 2 holds FOLD with confidence MEDIUM and mix shifted slightly toward CALL (80/20 vs Round 1's 75/25). The range-construction call: at THIS node — UTG small-bet (~22%) followed by HJ+CO flat-flat — BB's continuing range is constructed from (a) Tx made hands (JTo/QTo/KTs/ATs that completed), (b) 88-22 mid/small PPs with SDV, (c) two-pair-and-better draws (65s/54s/64s/76s set-mining), (d) OESD/gutter+BDFD combos (53s/57s/87s/97s), (e) suited A-highs WITH live backdoor flush (AcXc, AhXh on relevant suits), and finally (f) a thin frequency of offsuit broadway A-highs as defensive mix. AdJh sits at category (f) — the marginal segment. The key construction principle: BB already has stronger A-highs (suited with live BDFD) populating the defending grid, so AdJh is the natural folding edge of A-high. Mix math: pure FOLD over-folds slightly given UTG's 22% sizing requires only ~18% equity face-value and AJo's A-blocker does unblock some UTG broadway-air c-bets; pure CALL ignores the OOP-3-deep negative realization and reverse-implied catastrophe on J/A turns. 80/20 reflects: 80% FOLD because (i) HJ and CO both flatting compresses villain composition toward made hands (a pure-air c-bet rarely gets two flats on T64r), (ii) realization 0.70-0.75 drags raw 20-22% to realised 15-17%, (iii) hero is OOP-3-deep with squeeze-pressure-against on every future street, (iv) BDFD is essentially dead on rainbow with one Ad; 20% CALL because (i) face-value pot odds clear, (ii) A-blocker has nonzero unblock value vs UTG's tiny-sizing broadway-air, (iii) closing-action this street gives a free single-street look. Sonnet majority CALL is wrong because they double-count overcard outs without discounting for dirty turns. Peer FOLDs and Opus tier-up FOLD all converge: FOLD is modal, CALL is the live defensive mix at low frequency.
